items.question: What does '2 teams sign' mean?
items.text: "2 teams sign" means a decision is Tier 3: two approvers from two different teams must both sign before it goes ahead. The person who proposed the decision can't be one of the signers, so a second pair of eyes always checks it. You'll see these on the Decisions page, where each waiting decision shows who must sign and its decide-by time. The button below opens that page.

items.question: Was bedeutet ETR?
items.text: ETR steht für "Estimated Time of Restoration", also den voraussichtlichen Zeitpunkt, zu dem die Kundinnen und Kunden wieder Strom haben. Die Plattform nennt dafür einen Mittelwert (Median) und einen Bereich. Es gibt eine globale ETR für das gesamte System, nämlich wenn 90 % der Kunden mit dem Spitzenwert der Ausfälle wieder versorgt sind, und eine ETR pro Gebiet für jeden Einsatzbereich. Wie genau frühere Schätzungen waren, sehen Sie im Reiter "ETR accuracy" auf der After-action-Seite, die der Button unten öffnet. Die tatsächlichen Werte sind dort simuliert, das ist also Übung und kein Feldnachweis.

turns: Should the published ETR be revised?
items.question: Why?
items.text: The published ETR (issued Sep 28, 13:30 ET) may need revising because the county total is falling, now 168,598 customers out against a peak of 1,604,454, which may not match the published median restoration estimate of 79.4 h. Several crews are still enroute, and the network map feed is stale. Outage surge signals to check in counties flagged exceeds_mcc may be data dropouts, so treat them cautiously. Per-county ETRs and per-feeder restoration times are missing.
prior_answers:
The evidence cannot settle this, because it holds no current median restoration estimate to compare against the published estimate. The published global ETR was issued at Sep 28, 13:30 ET, with a median restoration estimate of 79.4 h. DOM 14.206 requires a revision when the median moves by more than the margin it sets, and smaller moves are logged but not released. [1] As ETR Specialist you propose any revision on F-DOM-121, and the Incident Commander and the Duty Manager sign it. [2] County customers out are 168,598 and falling.

Sources:
[1] DOM 14.206 Rev K, Revision Summary; 1.0 PURPOSE; 6.0 PROCEDURE, pp. 1-3: "6.4.2 Revise a published ETR when the P50 moves by more than 12 h.6.4.3 A move of 12 h or less is logged but not released."
[2] DOM 14.206 Rev K, Revision Summary; 1.0 PURPOSE; 6.0 PROCEDURE, pp. 1-3: "6.2.3 The ETR Specialist proposes the global ETR on F-DOM-121 with the model inputs attached.6.2.4 The Incident Commander and the Duty Manager approve the global ETR before release. Both signatures go on F-DOM-121."

answer.text: The published ETR (issued Sep 28, 13:30 ET) may need revising because the county total is falling, now 168,598 customers out against a peak of 1,604,454, which may not match the published median restoration estimate of 79.4 h. Several crews are still enroute, and the network map feed is stale. Outage surge signals to check in counties flagged exceeds_mcc may be data dropouts, so treat them cautiously. Per-county ETRs and per-feeder restoration times are missing.
